body.estimand_functional: For an established contraction chart, \(g_{\chi}(C_{\le R})=\beta=C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,Y]/C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,T]\) on \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\), and it returns \(\bot\) otherwise. For \(\ell=2\) and \(R\ge3\), the additional order-three map in the two-latent depth theorem returns \(-a_0(C_{\le3})/a_1(C_{\le3})\) when \(\det(M_3)a_1(C_{\le3})\ne0\), and returns \(\bot\) otherwise; here \(a_0,a_1\) are the displayed observable coefficients of \(\mathcal P_\zeta\).

sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. sampling from one fixed member of \(\mathcal M_{\ell}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention target is the structural edge coefficient \(\beta\) on \(T\to Y\); treatment is not randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used; regular inference is reported only when the deterministic selector returns an established chart whose discriminant is nonzero, while confidence-fiber inversion remains total at chart collisions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate all entries of \(C_{\le R}\) by multivariate \(k\)-statistics. The fixed degree-then-lexicographic selector returns \(\chi_n,d_n,\widehat\beta_n\) only on their declared established-chart domain and returns \(\bot\) otherwise. For collision-robust inversion, compute \(\widehat\mu_R\), \(\rho_n\), \(Q_n\), the possibly empty legal intersection \(\mathcal J_n\), the total projected set \(I_n\), and \(\eta_n\) from the finite atomic quantified-real presentation of \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\).

body.tldr: Higher-order cumulants identify the treatment effect in the fixed single-proxy latent-confounded LiNGAM, but the published order \(k(\ell)\) is only sufficient. The proved frontier now has exact depths \(r_\beta(1)=r_\beta(2)=3\) and \(r_\beta(3)=4\), global bounds with matching square-root asymptotics, and terminating algebraic recovery maps with explicit instability certificates. The mandatory complete \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) test has a linear target eliminant: on \(\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\), every legal representation has \(\beta=-a_0/a_1\), and the unequal-effect incidence saturation is empty. Exact finite depths for \(\ell\ge4\) remain open, beginning at \((4,3)\). The class bridge distinguishes the paper's centered, realizable finite-atomic truncation from Tramontano et al.'s larger unrestricted diagonal-cumulant chart while showing that finite-support converse twins transfer to their actual-law class and that the upper contraction algebra transfers to their generic chart.

project_justification.gap: Tramontano et al. prove proxy-effect identification through the bivariate recovery order \(k(\ell)\), with \(k(2)=6\), but do not determine the minimum depth of the complete ternary cumulant law. Their algebraic generic chart treats diagonal cumulants as unrestricted coordinates, whereas the present legal domain also enforces positive variances and simultaneous centered moment realizability. Before this result, the generically finite \((2,3)\) map left open a disconnected legal unequal-effect branch.
project_justification.niche: The graph's distinguished treatment and outcome disturbance directions allow a mixed covariance identity to be interpolated through the invertible proxy-anchored third-cumulant matrix. For two latents this produces a linear observable target eliminant even though no degree-one proxy annihilator exists.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves \(r_\beta(2)=3\) by the explicit map \(-a_0/a_1\), certifies the exceptional locus by \(\det(M_3)a_1=0\), and proves that the localized unequal-effect incidence ideal is empty. Together with the established one- and three-latent cases, the exact values are now three, three, and four for \(\ell=1,2,3\). The global bounds and square-root asymptotics remain, while exact intermediate-order classification for \(\ell\ge4\) is retained as the honest frontier. For the companion implementation, the two-latent minimum input falls from the published sufficient order six to order three and gains a determinant-slope instability report.

body.related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025, Theorem 3.1) use a degree-\(\ell+1\) bivariate loading-root polynomial through \(k(\ell)\); Theorems 3.4--3.5 align the resulting proxy loading lists and prove effect sufficiency at that order. Their unrestricted diagonal-cumulant parameterization is the algebraic ambient chart, while the present \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\) is a centered, generic-nonzero, actual-law truncation with positive variance and simultaneous cross-order realizability. The class bridge shows exactly what transfers in each direction. For \(\ell=2\), the published workflow uses \(k(2)=6\), whereas the new complete-tensor identity gives the sharp order three and rules out a separate nonsingular legal target branch. For \(\ell=3\), the established sharp order is four rather than \(k(3)=7\). Theorem 3.6 of Tramontano et al. claims order-three nonidentification for one latent; the established one-latent theorem instead gives order-three full-fiber recovery and audits the extra algebraic root under the legal moment-domain restrictions. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024) supply the bivariate root machinery, while Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010) supply the target-elimination viewpoint; neither gives the mixed covariance--third-cumulant linear target certificate proved here. Full-distribution overcomplete independent-component results and the banked bivariate causal-direction frontier concern different targets and do not settle this fixed-graph minimum complete-cumulant depth.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The contraction discriminant is initially a certificate-failure locus, not yet the true nonidentification locus. Accordingly, every chart-specific scalar construction returns \(\bot\) when its atlas is empty, its pivot or denominator vanishes, or its input lies outside the chart domain; no value on that failure locus is interpreted as an effect. The exact \(\ell=2,R=3\) real beta projection under the quantified finite-atomic source-moment constraints is the mandatory early decision. Complex fiber degree, Jacobian rank, failure of one annihilator, an unrestricted diagonal-cumulant solution, and a single finite-support witness are each insufficient for the global converse. The order-three algebraic image closure permits diagonal cumulant coordinates that need not be positive-variance centered source moments; polynomial degree alone therefore does not count legal preimages. Uniform confidence-fiber coverage uses the explicit observed-data envelope \(\lVert X\rVert_{\infty}\le M\); no observed bound is inferred from bounded latent sources or bounded disturbances with unrestricted structural coefficients. Off the simultaneous moment-coverage event the legal intersection and projected set may be empty and are reported as such. At an exact collision, honest coverage need not imply singleton contraction, and the limiting diameter is the legal-fiber modulus rather than a Wald rate.
body.honest_scope: The complete \((2,3)\) beta projection is settled on the explicit nonempty legal chart \(\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\): its target rational-univariate representation is linear over both the real and complex fibers, so there is no second positive-variance branch there. The result does not claim that the proxy-annihilator atlas itself works at order three for two latents; the new mixed covariance--third-cumulant map is a separate terminating chart and is included explicitly in the estimand functional. The established contraction theorem still supplies the all-\(\ell\) upper depth \(U_\ell\), and finite-support lower twins transfer to the published actual-law class, but the unrestricted diagonal algebraic chart is larger than the realizable moment domain. Exact depths for \(\ell\ge4\) and legal-real fibers at unresolved intermediate orders remain open, beginning with \((4,3)\). The bivariate causal-direction minimum-order frontier is distinct: it orients an arrow between two observed variables, whereas this paper fixes the single-proxy graph and identifies the interventional coefficient \(\beta\) from the complete trivariate cumulant map.
